paper_title: The Complexity of Homomorphism Reconstruction Revisited
classifications: Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: Question: Is there a graph G such that hom(Fi , G) = mi for every i ∈ [k]?
context: p-UnHomRec Input: Pairs (F1 , m1 ), . . . , (Fk , mk ), where F1 , . . . , Fk are graphs and m1 , . . . , mℓ ∈ N (in unary encoding). Pk Parameter: i=1 |Fi | Question: Is there a graph G such that hom(Fi , G) = mi for every i ∈ [k]? It is open if this problem is fixed-parameter tractable, or at least the complexity class XP, that is, solvable in polynomial time for each fixed parameter value. We prove that the problem is in XP if the Fi are stars.
